lessons.title: I froze as the hand on my shoulder turned icy, its fingers curling around my wrist like a dead child's grasp. My wife's voice trembled from the bed, "Honey, is the baby crying?" I turned to see her silhouette framed by the moonlight, eyes hollow and unblinking. The nursery monitor flickered, the lullaby warbling into a guttural moan. On the screen, the crib was empty—just a dark void where the baby should have been. A soft, wet giggle echoed from the hallway, and the temperature dropped further. I whispered, "Who's there?" The reply came from the darkness behind me: a child's breath, ragged and desperate, "Don't leave me, Daddy..." The hand tightened, pulling me toward the crib, and the last thing I saw was my wife's smile, cracked and dead, as the camera feed went black.
